findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how release-notes completeness is proven (e.g. derive the null->absent field list from a diff of old mirror defaults vs new omit-None bodies, or scope the AC to the enumerated tool families the wire tests cover).
evidence: 'docs/release-notes.md lists every field that was null and is now absent, per tool family.'

The Testing section lists wire tests (test_show_ticket_wire_payload_validates_with_absent_optionals, test_write_ack_omits_unset_advisories) that prove absence for specific tools, but nothing enumerates the full null->absent set across all tool families.
findings.finding: The final acceptance criterion requires release-notes to list 'every field that was null and is now absent, per tool family', but no proving command or check cross-validates that the list is COMPLETE — completeness of 'every field' is asserted, not measured.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — last bullet ('Non-codebase: docs/release-notes.md lists every field...')

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the non-discriminating ready_tickets anyOf: either gate the two row shapes by the `full` arg so each mode advertises exactly one schema, or make the lean-mode test assert a lean row with an injected extra key is REJECTED (not merely that both modes 'pass'), so the lean contract is actually enforced.
evidence: ready_ticket_summary.schema.json:7 `"additionalProperties": false`
ticket_state.schema.json:7 `"additionalProperties": true`
An anyOf whose second branch admits any object makes the validator accept a lean row with stray keys, so the lean/full distinction is not enforced by the advertised schema
Testing only asserts 'both modes pass the lowlevel validator' — true by construction once one branch is permissive
findings.finding: The ready_tickets outputSchema is an anyOf of ready_ticket_summary (additionalProperties:false) and ticket_state (additionalProperties:true); because the ticket_state branch is permissive, a lean default row that carries unexpected extra keys still validates against the ticket_state branch, so the advertised schema cannot actually enforce the lean contract and the proposed test ('both modes pass the lowlevel validator') is trivially satisfied by the open branch.
findings.location: Approach — 'ready_tickets (ready_ticket_summary, ticket_state): lean rows by default, full rows with full=true'; Testing — test_ready_tickets_full_and_lean_rows_validate
scenarios: A future change leaks an extra key into the lean ready_tickets row; the canonical outputSchema still validates it and no test catches the drift
The lean-vs-full contract the ready_tickets split exists to enforce is advertised but unenforceable

resolve_symbol could not confirm the instance fields (expected for instance attributes), leaving this UNVERIFIED rather than MISMATCH

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify verify_completion_status.verdict as a free-form string (or enumerate the full compute_validity vocabulary: certified, unsigned, stale-reopened, stale-material, not-closed, and any other classifier reasons) so the advertised schema accepts every value gate_runs.verify_completion_status emits.
evidence: Plan declares only field names: 'verify_completion_status (ok, verdict, reason; nullable verified_at_sha, signed_at)'

src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:377-418: verdict is `str(validity.get('verdict') or 'unsigned')` — 'certified only when valid RIGHT NOW, else the classifier reason (stale-reopened / stale-material / not-closed / unsigned / …)'
src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:189-191 docstring claims 'verdict is certified or unsigned', which contradicts the library's open-ended classifier reasons
jsonschema.validate against tool.outputSchema (per plan Context) will REJECT any real verdict value an enum omits
findings.finding: The new verify_completion_status schema declares a `verdict` field but never defines its value vocabulary; the live library emits an open-ended set (certified, unsigned, stale-reopened, stale-material, not-closed, …), so an under-specified or wrongly-enumerated verdict will fail the lowlevel validator the plan relies on.
scenarios: A client polls verify_completion_status for a reopened/stale ticket; verdict='stale-reopened' is returned and the SDK validator rejects the structured result at wire time.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `verdict` as `{"type": "string"}` (unconstrained) in verify_completion_status.schema.json, matching gate_runs.py's open-ended str() verdict, rather than an enum limited to certified/unsigned.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define gate_run.status to cover all five emitted values (running, passed, failed, attaching, unknown) — or declare it an unconstrained string — matching gate_runs.gate_run_status.
evidence: Plan declares only 'gate_run (job_id, status; …)' with no vocabulary for status
src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:320-343: status is 'running / passed / failed / attaching / unknown'; attaching and unknown are returned from bare `{job_id, status}` records without ticket_id/gate_type
findings.finding: The new gate_run schema lists `status` without stating its value vocabulary; the library emits five distinct values (running/passed/failed/attaching/unknown), so an enum that omits any (e.g. attaching, unknown) will reject real poll records.
scenarios: A follower polls gate_status before the leader's index write and gets status='attaching'; or an unrecognized job_id returns status='unknown'. If the schema's status enum omits these, the validator rejects the result.
findings.suggested_fix: If status is an enum in gate_run.schema.json, enumerate [running, passed, failed, attaching, unknown]; note attaching/unknown records carry only {job_id, status}, so ticket_id/gate_type must be optional (nullable+absent), as the plan already states for nullability.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (with an in-memory client assertion) that overwriting fn_metadata.output_schema changes BOTH the tools/list-advertised outputSchema AND the shape the lowlevel server validates/serializes structuredContent against, or specify how output_model is reconciled so the two surfaces cannot disagree.
evidence: test_mcp_js_safe_integers.py:172-179: 'FastMCP builds structuredContent with output_model.model_validate(...) (func_metadata.py:129)' — structuredContent is derived from output_model, not necessarily from output_schema

Plan cites 'jsonschema.validate against tool.outputSchema, mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:566-575' as the validation seam, implying output_schema drives validation, but the tools/list advertised outputSchema and the structuredContent-building model are two distinct SDK surfaces the plan treats as one

The plan keeps output_model non-None (asserts it) but replaces output_schema with hand-rolled JSON, risking a published outputSchema that disagrees with the model used to materialize/validate structuredContent
findings.finding: The plan assumes overwriting fn_metadata.output_schema re-advertises the schema to clients, but the SDK's existing behavior (observed in the repo) builds structuredContent by validating the result through output_model.model_validate(...); the plan does not reconcile how overwriting output_schema alone (while leaving/asserting a possibly-stale output_model) yields a client-visible outputSchema equal to the canonical file and still validates the returned dict.
findings.location: Approach: 'return the library payload unchanged' + 'sets ... fn_metadata.output_schema, asserting output_model is not None'
scenarios: A tool returns a dict with a key the stale output_model drops or coerces (e.g. the ns-timestamp int/str case the existing test guards), so structuredContent diverges from the advertised canonical outputSchema
findings.suggested_fix: Either set output_model to None (or a generic model) where kind demands it and prove via the in-memory session test that structuredContent is built from the overwritten output_schema, or document the exact FuncMetadata code path (validate vs serialize) so Pass-2 can confirm the published schema and the validated payload are the same object.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new schema file names with their OUTPUT_SCHEMAS keys (name the file gate_status/attach_commits, or state the key->file mapping explicitly so the canonical-diff test keys correctly).
evidence: 'New: write_ack (...), attach_commits_result (...), gate_run (...), verify_completion_status (...)'
'wire the new files into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS under keys attach_commits, gate_status, verify_completion_status, write_ack'
findings.finding: The four new schema FILES are named write_ack, attach_commits_result, gate_run, verify_completion_status, but they are wired into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS under KEYS attach_commits, gate_status, verify_completion_status, write_ack — the file name 'gate_run' maps to key 'gate_status' and 'attach_commits_result' maps to key 'attach_commits', a name drift that the canonical-diff test keys against.
findings.location: Approach — 'New: write_ack ..., attach_commits_result ..., gate_run ..., verify_completion_status ...' vs 'wire the new files into OUTPUT_SCHEMAS under keys attach_commits, gate_status, verify_completion_status, write_ack'
scenarios: test_every_advertised_output_schema_equals_its_canonical_file resolves a key ('gate_status') that does not match the schema file name ('gate_run'), or vice versa, causing a lookup miss or an unintended cross-reference.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify inline_schema() against the existing schemas.registry()/schemas.validator() referencing.Registry precedent — state the actual SDK-side constraint (the MCP lowlevel server validates against tool.outputSchema with its own validator and no supplied registry) that forces self-contained schemas, rather than citing a generic 'jsonschema.validate cannot resolve cross-file refs' limitation the repo already works around.
evidence: src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:431-444 `registry()` builds a `referencing.Registry` so 'cross-file $refs (e.g. common.schema.json#/$defs/comment) resolve'
src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:447-451 `validator(name)` wires the cross-file registry in, explicitly 'instead of jsonschema.validate(instance, load(name)) so $refs to common resolve'
Web (python-jsonschema/jsonschema#382; StackOverflow 60949065) corroborates that bare jsonschema cross-file $ref resolution is a known pain point — but the repo's answer is a Registry, not inlining

The real constraint is SDK-side: the MCP lowlevel server builds its own validator around tool.outputSchema, so a plain self-contained schema may genuinely be required — but the plan never states this as the reason, instead citing a jsonschema limitation the repo already works around
findings.finding: The plan introduces inline_schema() to resolve cross-file $refs by hoisting common.schema.json#/$defs/* into local $defs, justified by 'jsonschema.validate cannot resolve cross-file refs', but the repo already ships a prior-art mechanism for the same problem (schemas.registry()/schemas.validator() build a referencing.Registry that resolves those exact refs) and the plan never considers or justifies inlining over it.
findings.location: Approach — 'inline_schema(names, kind) hoists common.schema.json#/$defs/* into local $defs ... (jsonschema.validate cannot resolve cross-file refs)'
scenarios: Reviewer or implementer asks why the inlining helper duplicates logic the schemas package already provides via referencing.Registry
Future drift between the two ref-resolution strategies (inline copy of $defs vs the Registry used by schemas.validator) if common.$defs changes
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the parenthetical rationale with the SDK-side reason inlining is unavoidable (the MCP SDK constructs its validator around tool.outputSchema without a referencing.Registry, so advertised schemas must be self-contained), and note why schemas.registry()/validator() cannot be reused at that boundary.
